statusText: About 30 minutes before the Friday U.S. cash close (20:00 UTC): the confirmed August UMich consumer-sentiment miss (51.0 vs ~54.5 consensus) and the already-absorbed July Retail Sales drop (-0.6% MoM) remain fully digested, but a fresh, confirmed earnings-driven catalyst has emerged since the last run -- Broadcom fell roughly 5-7% intraday on investor concern that its shift toward lower-margin custom AI silicon will pressure margins, and Applied Materials fell about 5% despite record Q3 revenue, as its post-July rally left no room for anything short of a blowout. Both are large Nasdaq-100 weights and are the primary reason the Nasdaq-100 (-0.4%) is underperforming the S&P 500 and Dow (both -0.2%) today. This reads as earnings-specific, single-name dispersion rather than a coherent index-level directional move: SanDisk and Western Digital are firm (+5-6%, +1-2%), and reports on AMD are conflicting across sources (one describes AMD up as much as 5% on its well-received bond issuance, another describes AMD trimming losses alongside the broader chip-equipment slide) -- consistent with a mixed, non-directional tape rather than aligned cross-asset confirmation. NQ futures continue trading within the broad multi-hour range established earlier in the session; sourcing on the precise current tick is inconsistent (one snapshot near 18:07 UTC showed 30,263.62 against a wider full-session range down to 29,780.50, while the last hour's confirmed narrower range was 30,124.25-30,232.00), so no authoritative single fresh NQ print is available this run, but no failed-pullback or repeated-extension structure has been identified in any source. VIX holds calm near 14.6 (today's range about 14.39-14.80). The 10-year Treasury yield is up roughly 5bp to about 4.69%, attributed by reporting to the soft retail sales print plus a fresh U.S. statement that its naval blockade of Iranian ports could continue "indefinitely." The 2-year yield again has no fresh confirmed print this run and is carried forward as stale. WTI holds flat near $81.3 (range $80.77-82.99); Brent is firmer near $87-88. On the Strait of Hormuz, further reporting confirms the Thursday-evening attack involved two UAE-linked ADNOC tankers plus a separate drone strike on a tanker exiting the strait (UK Maritime Trade Operations, minor damage, no casualties), with Qatar, Kuwait, Egypt and Bahrain condemning Iran -- incremental confirmatory detail on an already-known, multi-week-old crisis rather than a fresh discrete escalation. Alpha Vantage's free-tier daily quota remained exhausted this run (one call plus one retry, both rate_limit errors); direct financial-data site fetches (investing.com, cnbc.com) were again blocked by the network egress proxy, so this run again relies entirely on WebSearch snippets, with reasonable cross-source corroboration on the index moves, VIX, yields, oil, the semis story and the Hormuz detail, but no single authoritative fresh NQ tick and no fresh 2-year yield print.
recommendation: Current action remains EA_ON. Tail edges up slightly to 9% (still low) to reflect the newly confirmed Broadcom/Applied Materials earnings-driven weakness, which is a real, large-weight index-level drag -- but it is earnings-specific single-name dispersion (offset by strength in SanDisk/Western Digital and conflicting AMD reports), not an observed persistent one-way NQ price-path reaction, so it does not meet the bar for an elevated Tail read. Stress edges up slightly to 41% (moderate, upper band) from 40% last hour, reflecting the added semis-sector earnings volatility layered on the persistent Hormuz thread and the modest yield rise, while VIX itself stays calm. Confidence firms slightly to 43% (medium-low) from 42% on reasonable cross-source corroboration of the new semis story and Hormuz detail, offset by the continued Alpha Vantage outage, blocked direct-data fetches, and an inconsistent NQ tick across sources. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain active regardless of the current EA_ON state. An upgrade to a higher Tail state would require an observed failed-pullback/repeated-extension reaction in NQ itself -- not the standing data misses, the semis earnings dispersion, or the Hormuz coverage/rhetoric on their own.
headline: Broadcom (-5 to -7%) and Applied Materials (-5% despite a beat) emerge as the session's dominant, confirmed earnings-driven drag on the Nasdaq-100 (-0.4%, underperforming the S&P 500/Dow's -0.2%) into the final half-hour before the Friday close; VIX stays calm (~14.6), NQ holds its established range, and SanDisk/Western Digital hold firm, keeping the tape mixed rather than directional.
body: At 19:31 UTC, about 30 minutes before the Friday U.S. cash close (20:00 UTC), the confirmed August UMich consumer sentiment miss (51.0 vs ~54.5 consensus, down from 55.2 in July) and the already-absorbed July Retail Sales drop (-0.6% MoM vs +0.1% expected) remain fully digested from earlier in the session. A fresh, confirmed catalyst has emerged since the prior run: Broadcom fell roughly 5-7% intraday on investor concern that its rapid shift toward lower-margin custom AI accelerators and networking hardware will pressure blended margins even as underlying AI demand stays robust, and Applied Materials fell about 5% despite record fiscal Q3 revenue of $9.12 billion and above-consensus guidance, as its sharp rally since July 29 (roughly +22%) left the stock priced for perfection heading into the print. Both are large Nasdaq-100 constituents and are the primary reason the Nasdaq-100 is underperforming today (-0.4%) relative to the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average (both -0.2%); the S&P 500 information technology sector is down about 0.5% on the day. This reads as earnings-specific, single-name/sector dispersion rather than a coherent index-level directional move: data-storage names SanDisk and Western Digital are firm (+5.6-5.7% and +1.4-2%, respectively, on SanDisk's Investor Day), and reporting on AMD is directly conflicting across sources -- one account describes AMD up as much as 5% on its well-received investment-grade bond issuance and reassuring long-term growth commentary, while another describes AMD, Intel and Micron trimming losses alongside a broader chip-equipment-led sell-off sparked by the Broadcom reaction. Given this conflict, AMD's specific move is treated as unresolved this run rather than asserted either way. NQ futures continue trading within the broad multi-hour range established earlier in the session; sourcing on the precise current tick is inconsistent between search snippets (one near 18:07 UTC showed 30,263.62 against a full-session range as low as 29,780.50, while the prior run's confirmed narrower session range was 30,124.25-30,232.00), so no single authoritative fresh NQ print is available this run -- but critically, no source describes a failed-pullback or repeated-extension reaction in NQ itself. VIX holds calm near 14.6 (today's reported range about 14.39-14.80), essentially unchanged from the prior run and from most of today's session. The 10-year Treasury yield is up roughly 5 basis points to about 4.69% today, with reporting attributing the move to both the soft retail sales print and a fresh U.S. statement that its naval blockade of Iranian ports could continue "indefinitely" -- a modest incremental escalation in official rhetoric, though still not a confirmed new price-transmission shock into equities. The 2-year Treasury yield again has no fresh confirmed print available this run and is carried forward as stale. WTI crude holds essentially flat near $81.3 (today's range $80.77-82.99), while Brent remains firmer (roughly $87-88) on the regionally-concentrated Hormuz risk premium; oil has not broken out of its recent range. On the Strait of Hormuz situation, further reporting today confirms the Thursday-evening attack involved two UAE-linked ADNOC tankers (UAE called it 'piracy', a violation of UN Security Council resolution 2817 per Qatar) plus a separate drone strike on a tanker exiting the strait reported by the UK Maritime Trade Operations (minor damage, no casualties, no oil spill), with Qatar, Kuwait, Egypt and Bahrain all issuing condemnations of Iran. This is incremental confirmatory detail layered onto an already-known, multi-week-old regional crisis rather than a fresh discrete escalation, and equity/oil-market transmission remains contained. Alpha Vantage's free-tier daily quota remained exhausted this run: one TREASURY_YIELD call and one retry both returned rate_limit errors, so per the economical-use instruction no further Alpha Vantage calls were attempted and no Alpha Vantage data was used. Direct financial-data site fetches (investing.com, cnbc.com) were again blocked by the network egress proxy, so this run again relies entirely on WebSearch snippets -- with reasonable cross-source corroboration on the index-level moves, VIX, yields, oil, the new semis story, and the Hormuz detail, but no single authoritative fresh NQ tick, no fresh 2-year yield print, and conflicting reports on AMD specifically. Tail edges up to 9% (still low) to reflect the newly confirmed, large-weight semis earnings drag, but stays low because it is earnings-specific dispersion (offset by SanDisk/Western Digital strength and unresolved AMD reporting) rather than an observed persistent one-way NQ price-path reaction. Stress edges up to 41% (moderate, upper band) from 40% last hour as the new semis-sector earnings volatility layers onto the persistent Hormuz thread and the modest yield rise, while VIX itself stays calm. Confidence firms slightly to 43% (medium-low) from 42% on reasonable corroboration of the new semis and Hormuz detail, offset by the continued Alpha Vantage outage, blocked direct-data fetches, an inconsistent NQ tick, and conflicting AMD reporting.

lookbackSummary: Tail held in the low band (7-16%) through the trailing 24 hours, easing from Thursday evening's post-CPI/PPI digestion into a stable single-digit floor through Friday's Asian/European session, then holding 7-9% through today's confirmed UMich and Retail Sales misses and, in the most recent hour, the newly confirmed Broadcom/Applied Materials earnings-driven semis drag. Stress ran from the upper-30s Thursday evening down to a low of 23% in the early Friday Asian session, rebuilt through the European morning into the confirmed UMich print (peaking near 44%), then held roughly flat around 40-41% through the U.S. afternoon as the data digested further without a confirmed equity-market breakdown, with the standing Strait of Hormuz crisis (multi-vessel tanker/drone attacks, regional condemnations) providing a persistent, contained event-importance driver throughout.
outlookSummary: Tail is projected to stay low (2-9%) through the next 24 hours: it eases toward 5-7% into the Friday cash close as today's earnings-driven semis dispersion stops actively repricing once the session ends, then drops to a low weekend floor (~2%) once NQ futures enter the CME weekend maintenance halt around 22:00 UTC. Stress is projected to resume easing from today's moderate band through the remainder of the U.S. session and into the close, then decay toward a low single-digit weekend floor as NQ enters the halt, held there by the absence of any active session rather than a resolved risk picture -- the standing Strait of Hormuz crisis remains the principal source of weekend headline/gap risk into Sunday's ~22:00 UTC reopen. No forecast slot currently implies an action change from EA_ON. Confidence is projected to decay gradually from the low-40s toward the mid-20s as the horizon moves away from this run's live evidence and, further out, away from any live trading session at all.
